clauses.statement: src/pr-manager.js's walkFiles(dir) walks the directory tree with an explicit pending queue and a single files accumulator; it does not recurse per directory or pass an accumulated subtree result as spread call arguments, so the walked file count never enters a call's argument list.
clauses.rationale: The previous implementation was files.push(...await walkFiles(fullPath)); once a subtree accumulates more entries than V8 accepts as call arguments this throws 'Maximum call stack size exceeded', the same failure class PR #409 fixed for 8 other walkers but did not cover for this one.

clauses.statement: Given a subtree containing more entries than V8's spread-argument limit for the running stack size, when pr-manager.js's walkFiles processes it through its explicit-queue traversal flow -- moving each pending directory through a queued state then a processed state exactly once -- verified in a child process at --stack-size=200 with 30000 files (where the previous recursive+spread implementation throws 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'), then walkFiles returns the full flat file count without throwing RangeError.
clauses.rationale: Pins the regression at a suite-friendly scale: the reduced stack size scales the reproduction down from the real-world scale (280,852 files under .claude/worktrees) to 30000 files while exercising the identical failure mechanism (call-argument count, not recursion depth).

clauses.statement: architecture-profiler.js, code-quality-scanner.js, and database-access-scanner.js each point their local IGNORED_DIRS/PROFILER_IGNORED_DIRS identifier at the single shared src/scan-ignored-dirs.js SCAN_IGNORED_DIRS facade instead of maintaining an independent Set literal, so the three scanners' ignore sets cannot drift apart the way they had (architecture-profiler ignored .worktrees, the other two did not; none ignored .claude).
clauses.rationale: SCAN_IGNORED_DIRS is exposed as a frozen has()-only object, not a frozen Set, because Object.freeze on a Set only freezes the Set object's own properties, not its internal slots, so .add()/.delete() would still mutate the one shared instance across all three consumers.

  CLI[check architecture / story diagnose] --> Profiler[architecture-profiler collectFiles]
  CLI --> Quality[code-quality-scanner collectFiles]
  CLI --> DbAccess[database-access-scanner collectFiles]

diagrams.rationale: Shows both changed surfaces of this Story on one diagram: the three scanners now sharing one ignore-set check, and pr-manager's walkFiles now using the same iterative pending-queue shape as the scanners' own collectFiles walkers.

diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Actor[Contributor placing or leaving source under an ignored dir name] --> Surface[SCAN_IGNORED_DIRS: .claude / .worktrees / node_modules / etc.]
  Mutator[Hypothetical call site invoking .add or .delete] --> Surface
  Surface --> Asset[architecture-profiler / code-quality-scanner / database-access-scanner findings feeding VibePro gate evidence]
  Threat1[Threat: real source hidden under an ignored dir evades detection] --> Surface
  Threat2[Threat: shared set mutated at runtime, scanners silently drift apart] --> Surface
  Surface --> Control1[has-only frozen facade structurally blocks add/delete mutation]
  Surface --> Control2[Ignore set limited to tooling/session-state dir names, never product source dir names]
  Control1 --> Asset
  Control2 --> Asset
diagrams.rationale: The only security-relevant surface this Story touches is scan-scope narrowing: a scanner that silently under-scans produces a misleadingly clean finding set for the gates that consume it (architecture axis quality, responsibility-authority candidates, code-quality risk surfaces). The has()-only frozen facade and the tooling-only exclusion list are the two controls that keep that narrowing bounded and non-driftable.
